cards.text: Joshua, Israel's leader, dismisses the people. The Israelites head out to take possession of the land, each one to his own inheritance. After years in the back of a junk drawer, if somebody handed ME my own land, I'd hop there so fast my gold base would leave skid marks!

cards.question: All through Joshua's days, the people serve the LORD.
The people keep serving the LORD even after Joshua. Through the days of whom?

answers.text: The priests who carried the ark
The kings who ruled after Joshua

cards.question: Those elders had ___ all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.

cards.text: Then Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, dies at the age of 110. A HUNDRED AND TEN, and I'm out of breath after hopping my gold base from one oven to the next!

cards.question: Everybody went to their own inheritance. So where do they bury Joshua?

answers.text: In the land of his own inheritance
Back at the camp in Gilgal

cards.text: Then that whole generation, the ones who saw it all, is gathered to their fathers. And another generation rises up.

cards.question: What's different about this new generation?

answers.text: They did not know the LORD or His works
They did not know the land of their inheritance
They did not know which tribe they came from

cards.question: This new generation serves the LORD just like the elders did.

cards.text: They do evil in the sight of the LORD and serve Baal and the Ashtoreths. They follow the gods of the peoples around them and bow down to them.

cards.question: They forsook the LORD, the God of their ___, who had brought them out of the land of ___.

cards.text: All this provokes the LORD to anger, and His anger burns against Israel. He delivers them into the hands of those who plunder them.

cards.question: How does Israel do now against their enemies all around them?

answers.text: They can no longer resist them

cards.question: Wherever Israel marches out, what is the hand of the LORD doing?
This calamity comes just as the LORD had sworn to Israel.

cards.text: So Israel is greatly distressed. I know that feeling, friend: every time the junk drawer rattled open, I held my breath so hard my mustache stood straight up!
Hold on, friend. HOLD ON. Israel's in deep trouble, but the LORD isn't finished with them. He raises up judges.

cards.question: What do the judges the LORD raises up do?

answers.text: Write down new laws for Israel

cards.question: Israel listens to their judges.

cards.text: Instead, they prostitute themselves with other gods and bow down to them. And they don't take long to do it, either.

cards.question: They quickly turned from the way of their ___, who had walked in obedience to the LORD's commandments.

cards.text: So here's how it goes, friend. Whenever the LORD raises up a judge, and I mean EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. He's with that judge and saves Israel from their enemies as long as that judge is alive.

cards.question: Why does the LORD keep rescuing Israel?

answers.text: He is moved to pity by their groaning
They tear down the altars of Baal
The judges make a new covenant

cards.question: But what happens to Israel when the judge dies?

answers.text: They grow even more corrupt than their fathers
They turn back to the LORD for good
They ask for a king to rule them

cards.text: They won't give up their evil practices and stubborn ways. It's me and the snooze button, friend: every time I hit it, I sink DEEPER into the pillow!
Now it gets quiet, friend. Real quiet. The anger of the LORD burns against Israel, and He speaks: this nation has broken the covenant He laid down for their fathers and hasn't listened to His voice.

cards.question: The LORD says He will no longer drive out before them any of the ___ Joshua left when he died.
Why does the LORD say He's leaving those nations in place?

answers.text: To test whether Israel will walk in His way
To pay tribute to Israel every year
To show Israel how to farm the land

cards.text: Ohhh. So THAT's why the LORD had left those nations in place. He hadn't driven them out right away by handing them over to Joshua.

The LORD left these nations to test all the Israelites who had never known any of the wars in Canaan. The only war I ever knew was the dead batteries in my old drawer arguing over who had the most charge left!

cards.question: These nations were also left to teach ___ to later generations of Israel who had not known it.

cards.text: Here's the lineup: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites up in the mountains of Lebanon. And I thought the back of a junk drawer was crowded!

cards.question: The nations are there to find out whether Israel will keep the commandments the LORD gave their fathers through Moses.

cards.text: So the Israelites keep living among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. That's six peoples, friend, and Israel is right in the middle of all of them.

cards.question: Living side by side with these peoples, what do the Israelites end up doing?

answers.text: Marrying into them and serving their gods
Driving them out of the land at last
Teaching them the ways of the LORD

findings.problem: The earlier cards establish only that the elders outlived Joshua and that Israel served the LORD. They give no basis for choosing whether the elders had seen, forgotten, or recorded the works, so this asks the baker to guess wording that has not been shown.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions Egypt or the exodus, so the second blank especially cannot be reasoned out from the walkthrough. The baker must recall or guess unseen BSB wording rather than reason about the moment.
